titulo: Hacer / mandar + infinitive = to have something done
subtitulo: Mandé hacer un vestido. Se hizo construir una casa.
regla: Mandar + infinitive (very common in Mexico) and hacer + infinitive = to have something done by someone else, who isn't mentioned: Mandé hacer un vestido para la boda. Me hice construir un cuarto. Implies you arranged, ordered or paid for it.

bloques.texto: Someone else does the job; who doesn't matter. You **arranged or paid** for it.
**Mandar hacer** is everyday Mexican Spanish: **mandé hacer unas llaves**, **mandamos pintar la casa**.
In history or news, the subject may simply appear as the doer: **el rey construyó un palacio** (he had it built).
Tip: **mandar** = you gave the order, someone else did the work.

lista.es: ==Hicieron pintar== el departamento otra vez porque no les gustó cómo quedó.
lista.en: They had the apartment painted again because they didn't like how it turned out.

lista.es: ==Me hice construir== un cuarto extra para las visitas.
lista.en: I had an extra room built for guests.

lista.es: Voy a ==mandar hacer== un vestido para la boda de mi hija.
lista.en: I'm going to have a dress made for my daughter's wedding.
I had copies of the keys made.

lista.nota: Both are correct; **mandar a hacer** is very common in Mexico.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I'm going to have a cake made._
lista.r: Voy a mandar hacer un pastel.

lista.p: In Spanish: _They had the roof repaired._
In Spanish: _She had a house built._
lista.r: Se hizo construir una casa. / Mandó construir una casa.
